verdicts.explanation: Section 3.1 states that the lowest of the 9 Li-ion pathways for Livac t-LBO has Em = 0.46 eV, giving an estimated σion = 7.0 × 10−5 S cm−1; the value is DFT-derived, no temperature is given, and the secondary fields are null.

Section 3.1 gives σion = 7.6 × 10−8 S cm−1 for Ovac t-LBO as estimated in the authors' previous DFT work (Ref. [26]); the record's computational origin and null temperature are consistent with the paper.
Section 3.2 recalls σion = 7.0 × 10−13 S cm−1 for Livac m-LBO from Ref. [26]; the value, material and computational origin match, and there is no temperature.
Section 3.2 states Bvac m-LBO has the highest Li-ionic conductivity, σion = 2.8 × 10−2 S cm−1, from Ref. [26]; the material, value, unit and null temperature are correct.
Section 3.2 gives σion = 6.1 × 10−6 S cm−1 for Ovac m-LBO from Ref. [26]; the material, value, unit and null temperature are correct.

The introduction cites Hirose et al. [24] for total conductivity ca. 10−6 S cm−1 for t-LBO measured by EIS between 450 and 520 K, so literature_cited, total kind, the range (not a single temperature) and the high-pressure synthesis are all supported.
